detail.body:
## What does this PR do?

Align the GB300 DeepSeek V4 Pro performance recipe with the supplied full-model MCore run, and add 64-GPU GB300 and Rubin proxies matching the measured 16-block runs. The recipes support the development MCore APIs and require compatible native kernels; they are not qualified on Bridge's default MCore pin. The current validation target is public `dev` plus NVIDIA/Megatron-LM#5722, with the October 16 NeMo nightly image. Earlier completed GPU results below used the private `dsv4` pin `d211e50e888fcb8640ddc9923e98940800afcfd3`.

| Recipe | GPUs | Main logical blocks + MTP | TP / CP / EP | PP / VPP | Sequence | GBS / MBS |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---:|---|
| Full Pro | 256 | 61 + 1 | 1 / 16 / 64 | 4 / 4 | 65,536 | 256 / 1 |
| Proxy (GB300 / Rubin) | 64 | 16 + 1 | 1 / 16 / 64 | 1 / none | 65,536 | 256 / 1 |

The proxy keeps the full widths, expert geometry, attention/MoE kernels, and optimizer. It reduces GPU cost per iteration; it does not exercise PP/VPP or establish faster wall-clock steps.

## Changelog

- Restore the Rubin Pro proxy under the current `vrnvl72` recipe name, including the export and DSv4 step selector. It retains the GB300 proxy settings and the earlier Rubin run's MoK communication allocation of 40 SMs forward/backward. Legacy `vr200` launch input resolves through the existing alias.
- Initialize public MCore's DSA metric tracker before forward/graph capture, clear its storage in place between attempts, and reduce/report it on all participating ranks using the owning model's process groups. Preserve older runtimes without this lifecycle API.
- Set `is_hybrid_model=True` as native MCore does for hybrid patterns. This corrects initialization scaling and layer accounting; earlier Bridge runs inherited `False`, so the updated recipes do not reproduce their exact initial weights.
- Forward strict tokenizer-save error handling through the checkpoint compatibility wrapper instead of rejecting its keyword argument.
- Match the logged Pro architecture and `[3] + [4] * 14 + [2]` logical-block pipeline split; retain MTP in both recipes.
- Use layer-wise Muon, MXFP8 parameter gathering, FP32 gradient reduction, MoK/HybridEP, attention-only TE graphs, and selective MLA/mHC recompute with group size two. Disable activation offloading and paged stash.
- Add a fixed synthetic THD dataset with the logged pack shape, static boundary capacity, padding mask, and contiguous CP slicing. Preserve the dataset in the performance launcher and select the DSv4 forward step in both launch paths.
- Prepare development-MCore CP routes before the forward pass, and forward the layer-wise optimizer flag into DDP buffer construction while preserving the separate optimizer/DDP settings.
- Support the development MCore's legacy FSDP names and fixed rank-zero logging. Defer newer checkpoint APIs and reject unsupported GTP/tokenizer-asset requests explicitly; add focused compatibility tests. The first real container build exposed these missing imports.
- Add recipe/data/forward-step/optimizer regression tests and launch documentation. Require declared development-MCore capabilities instead of silently assigning unsupported fields.

Primary area: `area:recipe`. Related background: NVIDIA/Megatron-LM#5795.

## Public MCore dev validation

- Bridge commit: `0afea2b7cf53425a7188d63accdba2561c601c84`.
- MCore commit: `159e66cd2491b1bf4fdb0fa0895dd58f4dd9e4ed`, GitHub PR #5722's merge of `dev` `c0d3b03f584d07eb1ae94c576604cef4637c1be6` and PR head `944a5e617d7222fcc7e44cf187ac5473235233d2`. Using the old PR head alone would omit subsequent DSv4 fixes.
- Image: `nvcr.io/nvidian/nemo:nightly-2026-10-16`.
- Local validation: all pre-commit hooks passed; 38 focused DSA/checkpoint/logging unit tests passed; three isolated recipe capability/schema checks passed against the exact MCore merge source. Tests exercise the real adapter code with explicit external substitutes; GPU graph replay and distributed execution are not established by these tests.
- [GB300 proxy job 491427987](https://gitlab-master.nvidia.com/dl/JoC/nemo-ci/-/jobs/491427987), Slurm 3368946: all 50 steps completed with finite LM/MTP/indexer losses and gradient norms, zero skipped/NaN iterations, and Slurm SUCCEEDED. The log shows Muon/LayerWiseDistributedOptimizer and 17 graphable attention layers with capture followed by training. Mean step time over steps 41–50 was 27.36105 s. CI subsequently failed on the missing golden reference; this is a functional benchmark check, not convergence or numerical parity.
- [GB300 full pipeline 74364356](https://gitlab-master.nvidia.com/dl/JoC/nemo-ci/-/pipelines/74364356), [training job 491522880](https://gitlab-master.nvidia.com/dl/JoC/nemo-ci/-/jobs/491522880): submitted 256 GB300 / 61 main logical blocks + MTP / PP4-VPP4 for 50 steps, using Bridge `0afea2b7cf53425a7188d63accdba2561c601c84` and the same MCore/image as the completed public-dev proxy. Outcome pending.
- [Rubin proxy pipeline 74365644](https://gitlab-master.nvidia.com/dl/JoC/nemo-ci/-/pipelines/74365644): submitted 64 Rubin / 16 main logical blocks + MTP / PP1 for 50 steps, using Bridge `22b0b002d6627706386f8ba061a6bf216a4721d9`, the same MCore merge, and `nvcr.io/nvidian/nemo:rubin-devel-nightly-2026-10-16`. The Bridge delta restores the Rubin factory without changing GB300 runtime settings. Outcome pending.
- Both new runs use the cluster default Slurm account and default ntrace. The Rubin restoration passed all pre-commit hooks and 50 metadata tests; one unrelated Nemotron collision test also fails unchanged at the parent commit. The wrapper's executable body matches historical successful-run commit `8cc482ff3865b20cf24ecbc5374339b351f77077`; isolated selector/wrapper checks passed. Full framework tests require the cluster runtime.

MCore #5893's TE gradient-clone optimization remains absent from this public-dev merge. The native image also changed, so the earlier private-stack throughput and memory figures below are not performance guarantees for the new runtime.

## Earlier validation and private-runtime results

- 2026-10-15 merge with `main` (`d86a5c09b`): resolved the import/forward-step conflicts, preserved DSv4 fixed-THD routing across the online-packing refactor, and removed duplicate Muon DDP flag forwarding. `uv run pre-commit run --all-files` passed; 26 isolated packed-forward/DDP checks and seven fixed-THD data-contract checks passed. These execute source logic with explicit substitutes, not full framework imports or GPU training. Recipe-metadata/logging tests: 56 passed, with the same pre-existing unregistered Nemotron recipe collision failure noted below. The earlier GPU results predate this merge; GPU training has not been rerun. The secret scan flagged only two pinned MCore SHA literals in existing tests; the follow-up adds standard allowlist comments.
- `uv run pre-commit run --all-files`: passed, including the compatibility patch in [ARM container job 471532716](https://gitlab-master.nvidia.com/dl/JoC/nemo-ci/-/jobs/471532716).
- The derived DSv4 ARM image passed training imports, real Qwen recipe preparation, all 20 focused MCore compatibility tests, and native-runtime guards in [build 71863411](https://gitlab-master.nvidia.com/dl/JoC/nemo-ci/-/pipelines/71863411). Build/launch support is in [nemo-ci MR !2957](https://gitlab-master.nvidia.com/dl/JoC/nemo-ci/-/merge_requests/2957).
- [Eight-GB300 Qwen smoke](https://gitlab-master.nvidia.com/dl/JoC/nemo-ci/-/jobs/471613955): full 48-layer Qwen3-30B-A3B, BF16, EP 8, sequence length 512, MBS 1/GBS 8 completed five optimizer steps with finite loss/gradient norm and zero skipped/NaN iterations. Slurm succeeded; the GitLab job subsequently failed because this new short configuration has no convergence golden baseline. This validates generic training compatibility, not DSv4-specific kernels or performance.
- Source-only recipe metadata tests: 42 passed, with one pre-existing unrelated collision test deselected. The full file still reports the existing unregistered `nemotron_3_super_pretrain_64gpu_gb200_bf16_config` collision.
- Isolated production-source checks passed for capability guards/compression mapping, PP/CP metadata handling, CP-route fallback, and Muon DDP flag propagation. Model and optimizer assignments were checked against declared fields in the exact MCore revision and Bridge providers. These checks use lightweight substitutes and do not validate framework imports or GPU execution.
- [DSv4 CPU preflight job 471654045](https://gitlab-master.nvidia.com/dl/JoC/nemo-ci/-/jobs/471654045): 37 focused tests passed and two unsupported-MCore negative tests skipped because this development pin declares the required capabilities. Both proxy and full recipe preparation and fixed-THD sample checks completed before native validation. The CPU job failed only when MoK could not load the absent host driver library `libcuda.so.1`; a subsequent harness correction narrowly defers that exact error and was not rerun in CI. CPU checks stop before GPU-dependent configuration finalization, model construction, and training. The local macOS host still lacks the training dependencies.
- [Initial proxy job 471668742](https://gitlab-master.nvidia.com/dl/JoC/nemo-ci/-/jobs/471668742), [pipeline 71872319](https://gitlab-master.nvidia.com/dl/JoC/nemo-ci/-/pipelines/71872319), failed before its first completed optimizer step: a 600-second NCCL timeout in CP `_LeftBoundaryExchange.backward` / `batch_isend_irecv` at the pinned MCore's `csa_utils/cp_utils.py:194`. The root cause remains unestablished; the successful rerun does not establish a fix.
- [Instrumented proxy job 471754984](https://gitlab-master.nvidia.com/dl/JoC/nemo-ci/-/jobs/471754984), [pipeline 71884181](https://gitlab-master.nvidia.com/dl/JoC/nemo-ci/-/pipelines/71884181), completed all five optimizer steps on 64 GB300 GPUs; Slurm 3246221 SUCCEEDED. The resolved configuration matched the 16-block + MTP proxy, CP16/EP64, sequence 65,536, GBS256/MBS1, Muon and MXFP8. All five steps had finite LM, MTP, and reported auxiliary losses and gradient norms, with zero skipped/NaN iterations. LM loss changed from 13.20297 to 11.98748, MTP loss from 0.2063027 to 0.2020806, and gradient norms ranged from 1.005 to 4.521. A separate indexer-loss metric was not emitted. Rank 0 discovered 17 graphable attention layers and logged approximately 2.994 seconds of graph capture, followed by completed steps 2–5. GitLab failed after training: the convergence check had no golden reference, and ancillary reporting/artifact errors were also logged.
- The proxy passes the five-step functional acceptance gate. The initial 256-GPU full Pro submission, pipeline 71887633, was cancelled while queued; no training steps ran. Its replacement with default ntrace enabled passed the full-model functional checks described below. Diagnostic instrumentation was enabled for the successful proxy run, so its timings do not establish performance parity; convergence, numerical parity, all-rank memory coverage, and repeat-run performance remain unverified.

The synthetic dataset matches the fixed pack shape and uses new seeded random token inputs. The supplied MCore implementation derives an ascending mock-token stream; this source-derived behavior does not establish the exact runtime token tensors. The Bridge inputs do not reproduce that stream or the general variable-length packing scheduler. Forced load balancing and disabled benchmark NaN checks follow the measured runs; a completed benchmark is not a convergence or numerical-parity result.

## Before ready for review

- [x] Read contributor guidance; signed-off commit.
- [x] Added focused tests and launch documentation.
- [x] Run 20 focused MCore compatibility tests and the generic Qwen GPU smoke in the derived container.
- [x] Run the focused DSv4 CPU tests in the compatible container: 37 passed, two expected skips; driver-dependent validation deferred.
- [x] Complete the 64-GPU proxy five-step functional smoke, including graph capture and subsequent steps.
- [x] Complete the 50-step proxy and compare final steps 41–50 with common FLOP accounting.
- [x] Validate the 256-GPU full Pro run on GB300 with five finite steps and retained default ntrace capture (rank 0 / pipeline stage 0).



Proxy throughput accounting: Bridge reported about 850 model TFLOP/s/GPU at approximately the same 26.8-second step time as the supplied MCore proxy reporting about 1035. The pinned private MCore uses `o_lora_rank`/`o_groups`, while Bridge's FLOP estimator reads the newer output-projection field names. Consequently, the Bridge counter omits grouped output projections that the model actually executes. Normalizing both to the reference FLOP formula reconciles the figures; this is not evidence of a 20% runtime slowdown. Logged representative-rank peak reserved memory is 206.44 GB versus 206.60 GB in the reference after converting its MiB units. These are not maxima established across all 64 ranks.

The source audit also found an extra 1/64 scaling of the displayed MTP metric and missing indexer metric reporting in Bridge; shared MCore training computation/scaling is present. Input tokens differ (reference ascending, Bridge seeded random), and the external reference CPU-binding wrapper remains unaudited. No performance configuration changes or reporting-code fixes have been applied for this comparison.

The [50-step proxy baseline, job 471794923](https://gitlab-master.nvidia.com/dl/JoC/nemo-ci/-/jobs/471794923) ([pipeline 71888437](https://gitlab-master.nvidia.com/dl/JoC/nemo-ci/-/pipelines/71888437)) completed all 50 optimizer steps on 64 GB300 GPUs; Slurm 3246304 SUCCEEDED. The same image/source pins and model/batch settings were retained, with warmup0/decay50, ntrace explicitly disabled, and the extra NCCL flight-recorder diagnostics disabled. All 50 steps reported finite LM/MTP/auxiliary losses and gradient norms, with zero skipped/NaN iterations. Actual Muon/Newton–Schulz and 17 graphable attention layers were observed; graph capture was followed by completed steps 2–50. Final runtime configuration, allocation, and source-reference evidence matched the intended proxy. GitLab failed afterward because the convergence golden reference is missing; an ancillary executor-YAML copy warning was also logged.

| Final timing window: steps 41–50 | Bridge | Supplied MCore reference |
|---|---:|---:|
| Mean optimizer-step time | 25.85828 s | 26.84355 s |
| Common model TFLOP/s/GPU | 1072.868 | 1033.489 |
| Valid target tokens/s, global | 648,804 | 624,990 |

The shared FLOP numerator is 27.742519299 PFLOPs/GPU/step; sustained throughput divides total work by the summed ten-step time. Valid targets count GBS256 × 65,535 per step, excluding the padded position and not adding MTP targets. Bridge's mean step time was 3.67% lower and sustained throughput 3.81% higher in this single-run comparison. This does not establish a repeatable speed advantage, convergence, or numerical parity: the mock inputs differ, forced routing is enabled, and the reference CPU-binding wrapper is unavailable. No model/performance tuning or reporting-code changes were applied. The raw Bridge TFLOP counter still undercounts this private-MCore configuration.

At the user’s request, both configurations were relaunched with default ntrace enabled and the same image/source/model settings:

- [Proxy pipeline 71897205](https://gitlab-master.nvidia.com/dl/JoC/nemo-ci/-/pipelines/71897205): 64 GB300 GPUs, 16 main logical blocks + MTP, 50 steps.
- [Full Pro pipeline 71897247](https://gitlab-master.nvidia.com/dl/JoC/nemo-ci/-/pipelines/71897247): 256 GB300 GPUs, 61 main logical blocks + MTP, five steps, PP4/VPP4.

Both root pipelines were checked for `ENABLE_NTRACE=true`, the requested run lengths, and all three source pins. The earlier full Pro job 471783524 / Slurm 3246282 was cancelled while queued. The user explicitly requested the replacement launches above. No full-model training result exists from that attempt.

Default ntrace uses the nemo-ci gitlink `00f24c4f1076e1ca38b9c210193f236871405daf`, rank 0, four traced iterations (printed steps 2–5), stack/NVTX/memory diagnostics on, and Perfetto off. Separate NCCL flight-recorder diagnostics remain enabled for full Pro and disabled for the proxy. These runs are diagnostic; the accepted ntrace-disabled 50-step comparison above is preserved.

[The ntrace proxy job 471863037](https://gitlab-master.nvidia.com/dl/JoC/nemo-ci/-/jobs/471863037) completed all 50 optimizer steps; Slurm 3246625 SUCCEEDED. All 50 steps had finite LM/MTP/reported auxiliary losses and gradient norms, with zero skipped/NaN iterations. Automated and independent manual checks matched the configuration, 64-GPU allocation, and source records. Actual Muon/Newton–Schulz, 17 graphable layers, graph capture, and completed post-capture steps were observed. GitLab failed after successful training because the convergence golden reference is absent; an ancillary executor-YAML copy warning was logged, but the final executor artifact is present.

Ntrace capture and retention were verified beyond the enable flag: callback capture/save markers, CI postflight validation, all five expected nonempty files, Parquet metadata and rows, memory JSONL, and the generated HTML/JSON breakdown. The retained rank-0 data contains 1,466,996 rows: 8,704 capture-stack rows, 693,120 replay kernels, and 765,172 non-graph kernels. All 1,458,292 timed kernels have positive durations within four recorded iteration windows; nonnull Python/NVTX stack references resolve. The supplementary NVTX stack table and source manifest were also retrieved.

Trace attribution is limited: the generated breakdown labels 40.01% of root time as **No Python stack**. Replay kernel timings are present, but complete replay call-path reconstruction is not established by the retained capture. Coverage is rank 0 and printed steps 2–5 only; instrumented timings do not establish uninstrumented performance.

[Full Pro job 471863158](https://gitlab-master.nvidia.com/dl/JoC/nemo-ci/-/jobs/471863158) completed all five optimizer steps; Slurm 3246626 SUCCEEDED. Final saved configuration, allocation and source records match the requested 256 GB300 GPUs, 61 main logical blocks + one MTP, TP1/PP4/VPP4/CP16/EP64/ETP1, sequence 65,536, GBS256/MBS1, MXFP8, layer-wise Muon, HybridEP/MoK, mHC group two and attention graphs. The same derived image and three source revisions were retained. Automated and independent manual checks confirm finite LM/MTP/reported auxiliary losses and gradient norms at all five steps, with zero skipped/NaN iterations. LM loss changed from 13.20317 to 12.11772, reported MTP loss from 0.2063018 to 0.2030094, and gradient norms ranged from 1.146 to 8.117. Muon/Newton–Schulz execution was observed. Graph discovery counts for representative ranks 0/64/128/192 were 15/16/16/15; rank 0 logged 38.52047 seconds of capture followed by completed steps 2–5. A separate indexer-loss metric remains absent. GitLab failed afterward because convergence golden values are missing; this is separate from successful training.

Full Pro ntrace capture, save and CI retention were verified from the runtime events and retained data. All five default files plus the supplementary NVTX stack table and source manifest were retrieved and checked. Rank-0 records contain 1,285,336 rows: 7,680 capture-stack rows, 636,672 replay kernels and 640,984 non-graph kernels. All 1,277,656 timed rows have positive durations within the four windows corresponding to printed steps 2–5; all nonnull Python/NVTX references resolve. The generated breakdown assigns 32.00% of root time to **No Python stack**. Replay timings are retained, but the exact pinned matcher does not recover their Python call paths. This default capture covers only rank 0 / pipeline stage 0, not the full pipeline or every GPU.

The proxy and full Pro functional checks with default ntrace are complete. Five instrumented full-model steps do not establish convergence, numerical parity, or uninstrumented performance. Runtime source-reference evidence matches the requested pins, but this review does not independently attest every rank's source cleanliness or runtime image digest. The earlier unexplained proxy NCCL timeout remains unresolved; these successful runs do not identify its cause or establish a fix.

## Full Pro: 50-step follow-up

[Job 472022931](https://gitlab-master.nvidia.com/dl/JoC/nemo-ci/-/jobs/472022931), [root pipeline 71917884](https://gitlab-master.nvidia.com/dl/JoC/nemo-ci/-/pipelines/71917884), completed all 50 steps on 256 GB300 GPUs under Slurm account `coreai_mlperf_training`; Slurm 3247169 SUCCEEDED. Final artifacts preserve the validated 61-main-layer + MTP model, PP4/VPP4/CP16/EP64, sequence 65,536, GBS256/MBS1, MXFP8, Muon, HybridEP/MoK, mHC2, image and three source pins. Automated and independent manual checks found finite LM/MTP/reported auxiliary losses and gradient norms at every step, zero skipped/NaN iterations, actual Muon/Newton–Schulz and graph capture followed by completed updates. GitLab failed afterward because the convergence golden reference is missing.

| Printed steps 41–50 | Bridge | Supplied full MCore reference |
|---|---:|---:|
| Mean step time | 25.64042 s | 26.72270 s |
| Common model TFLOP/s/GPU | 926.231 | 888.718 |
| Valid target tokens/s, global | 654,317 | 627,817 |

The common numerator was recomputed for the full model (H31/C30/W1, 62 attention and MoE blocks including MTP): 23.748942609 PFLOP/GPU/step. This single-run observation is 4.05% shorter step time / 4.22% higher sustained throughput. Bridge's raw reported average is 750.87 TFLOP/s/GPU in this window; the legacy output-projection field mismatch still undercounts its model FLOPs. No reporting fix or tuning change was applied. Mock tokens differ and diagnostics were enabled, so these are not numerical-parity or repeatable-performance claims.

The matched early memory reports, after step 2 across 64 logged representatives, show 278.68 GB maximum reserved / 241.23 GB maximum allocated in Bridge versus 278.856 / 241.246 GB in the reference. These are not all-256-GPU maxima. The reference rises to 281.180 GB reserved later; Bridge has no matching late allocator samples.

Default ntrace capture and retained files passed row/window/reference/hash checks: 1,277,656 timed records cover rank 0 / pipeline stage 0 and printed steps 2–5 only. The breakdown leaves 31.81% of root time under No Python stack; replay timings are present but their Python attribution remains incomplete. The final-ten-step window is outside this capture. CI's separate `performance_flat` summary hardcodes printed steps 31–45 and therefore reports 25.86 s / 744.49 raw TFLOP/s/GPU; it does not use the requested 41–50 window. The values above were independently recomputed from the retained per-step logs.

+| `deepseek_v4_pro_pretrain_64gpu_gb300_fp8mx_proxy_config` | 64 | 16 | 1 / 16 / 64 | 1 / none | 256 / 1 |

+Both retain the Pro widths, expert count, one MTP module, 65,536-token sequence
+length, MXFP8 parameter gathering, and Muon with the `deepseekv4` coefficients
+and ten Newton–Schulz iterations. Each main logical block contains one attention
+layer and one MoE layer, so MCore reports 122 and 32 main physical layers,
+respectively. Both configurations have dense DP4, expert DP1, and 64
+microbatches per optimizer step. The full model splits its logical blocks across
+the sixteen VPP chunks as `[3] + [4] * 14 + [2]`.
+
+Both use selective `mla_up_proj` and mHC recompute with mHC group size two,
+Transformer Engine attention CUDA graphs with one warmup step and dynamic
+microbatches, and no activation offload or paged stash. The proxy reduces the
+allocation by four while retaining the long-context attention, MoE, mHC, MTP,
+and optimizer paths. Its PP1 schedule does not exercise the full recipe's
+pipeline communication or interleaved scheduling, and the smaller allocation
+does not guarantee a fourfold reduction in step time.
+
+Start with the proxy, then run the full recipe using the same runtime. With
+four GPUs per node, the canonical launches are:
+
+```bash
+./scripts/training/train.sh --nodes 16 --gpus-per-node 4 \
+  --recipe deepseek_v4_pro_pretrain_64gpu_gb300_fp8mx_proxy_config \
+  --mode pretrain
+
+./scripts/training/train.sh --nodes 64 --gpus-per-node 4 \
+  --recipe deepseek_v4_pro_pretrain_256gpu_gb300_fp8mx_config \
+  --mode pretrain
+```
+
+Use the account, partition, and container variables described above, and adjust
+the node count if the cluster exposes a different number of GPUs per node.
+These recipes own their mock dataset and 50-step benchmark schedule. Forced
+load balancing and disabled benchmark correctness checks mean a completed run
+is only an execution smoke test, not a convergence or numerical-parity test.
+For a stricter diagnostic run, enable `ddp.check_for_nan_in_grad=true` and
+`rerun_state_machine.check_for_nan_in_loss=true`; record those overrides when
+comparing performance.
+
+The launchers select `dsv4_step` automatically for these two recipes. The
+synthetic dataset emits fixed THD packed metadata, including boundaries on
+intermediate pipeline stages, with one full-length sequence per microbatch.
+It reproduces the fixed pack shape used in the logs, rather than their random
+token stream or the general variable-length `dp_balanced` data scheduler.

+        return None
+    try:

+    except ModuleNotFoundError as error:
+        if error.name != _DSA_LOGGING_MODULE:
+            raise

+    if not hasattr(dsa_logging, "initialize_dsa_metric_tracker"):

+        pg_collection: Process groups owning this model.

+    if not should_track:

+    # Discard state from an earlier in-process run, including its process groups.
+    dsa_logging.DSAIndexerLossLoggingHelper.tracker.clear()
